# Permissions

Keelson only reads, on every provider. Each provider's section lists the data a scan reads and what grants it:
a token permission on Cloudflare, a team role on Vercel, IAM actions on AWS, an App permission on GitHub.

## Cloudflare

The simplest token is Cloudflare's **Read all resources** template, which covers almost everything below.
Two sources need more:

- **Account API tokens** need *Account API Tokens Read*, which the template doesn't include.
- **Logpush jobs** can only be listed with a write permission, so Keelson doesn't list them; it reads Logpush health from GraphQL analytics instead.

A source the token can't read shows up under **Scans → Data coverage** with the permission it needs, and the checks that depend on it are
skipped rather than passed. Add accounts tests a token against each source before you connect it.

## Vercel

Vercel access tokens can't be limited to reading: a token can do whatever its user's role allows on each team it reaches.
Keelson only ever sends GET requests to Vercel (`test/vercel.test.ts` fails on anything else), and never asks for environment
variable values. A token created by a member with the **Viewer** role reads almost everything below; environment variable names,
the firewall configuration, drains and webhooks need a role that can see them. Create the token under **Account Settings → Tokens**,
scoped to the team you want to scan (or Full Account for every team), with an expiration date.

| Source | Who can read it | Checks that read it |
|---|---|---|
| Team settings | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-001, VID-008, VDP-007, VEN-006 |
| Team members and invitations | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-002, VID-003, VID-004 |
| Your access tokens | A Full Account token (a token scoped to one team can't list tokens) | VID-005, VID-006, VID-007 |
| Projects | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDP-001, VDP-002, VDP-003, VDP-004, VDP-005, VDP-006, VDP-008, VEN-008, VFW-002, VPL-001, VPL-002, VPL-003, VPL-004, VPL-006, VPL-005, XP-003 |
| Environment variable names and types | Developer, Member or Owner | VDP-008, VEN-001, VEN-002, VEN-003, VEN-004, VEN-005, VEN-007 |
| Project domains | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDP-002, VFW-002, VDM-002, XP-003 |
| Firewall configuration | Developer, Member, Security or Owner | VFW-001, VFW-002, VFW-003, VFW-004, VFW-005, VFW-006, VFW-007 |
| Domains | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDM-001 |
| Custom certificates | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDM-003 |
| Drains | Member or Owner | VMN-001, VMN-002, VMN-003, VMN-004 |
| Webhooks | Member or Owner | VMN-003 |
| Installed integrations | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-009 |
| Shared environment variable names and types | Developer, Member or Owner | Supporting data for other checks |

## AWS

An access key belongs to one AWS account, so each account needs its own. In each account, create an IAM user for Keelson,
attach AWS's managed **SecurityAudit** policy, and create an access key under **IAM → Users → the user → Security credentials**.
SecurityAudit reads configuration only: it can't change anything, and it can't read the objects in your buckets or the rows in your
databases. Temporary keys (the ones that start with ASIA) aren't accepted, because they expire within hours.

Keelson signs every request itself. It sends GET requests, and to services whose APIs only accept POST (CloudTrail, KMS, ECS and
others) only the read actions listed below; the client refuses any other action before sending it, and `test/aws.test.ts` fails on
anything else. It never asks for a secret's value, never stores a policy document, and scans environment variables and start-up
scripts for credentials in memory, keeping only the variable's name and the kind found. It keeps only the last four characters of an
access key ID. To recognise DNS records that point at AWS addresses it also
reads AWS's public address-range file, without the access key.

Regional sources are read in every region enabled for the account. A region that refuses the access key (a service control policy,
for example) is skipped and shown as not readable on the Regions page: nothing there is checked or counted as passing.

| Source | IAM actions | Checks that read it |
|---|---|---|
| Account identity | `sts:GetCallerIdentity` | Supporting data for other checks |
| IAM account summary (root user) | `iam:GetAccountSummary` | AID-001, AID-002 |
| IAM password policy | `iam:GetAccountPasswordPolicy` | AID-007 |
| IAM users, their access keys and MFA devices | `iam:ListUsers`, `iam:ListAccessKeys`, `iam:GetAccessKeyLastUsed`, `iam:ListMFADevices`, `iam:GetLoginProfile` | AID-003, AID-004, AID-005, AID-006, AID-007, AID-008 |
| IAM roles, groups and policies | `iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails` | AID-008, AID-009, AID-010, AID-011, AID-013, AEC-007, AID-012, XP-010, XP-011 |
| S3 Block Public Access for the account | `s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock` | AS3-001, AS3-002, AS3-003 |
| S3 buckets | `s3:ListAllMyBuckets`, `s3:GetBucketLocation` | AS3-001, AS3-002, AS3-003, ADN-001 |
| S3 bucket access settings | `s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock`, `s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus`, `s3:GetBucketAcl` | AS3-002, AS3-003 |
| Enabled regions | `ec2:DescribeRegions` | Supporting data for other checks |

## GitHub

Keelson reads GitHub as a GitHub App that you register and own: it isn't tied to a person, and each organization's owners see it under
**Settings → GitHub Apps**. Register it from the pre-filled link in Add accounts, which asks for the read-only permissions below and no
webhook, then install it on the organizations to scan and paste its App ID and private key into Keelson. One App covers every
organization it's installed on; to install a private App on more than one organization, make it public under its Advanced settings.

On each scan Keelson signs a short-lived token request with the private key and asks GitHub for an installation token with read access
to the permissions below and nothing else, so even an App that was given more can only read through Keelson. That request is the one
POST Keelson sends to GitHub; every other request is GET (`test/github.test.ts` fails on anything else). Secret scanning alerts are read
without the secret's value, and only the scheme and host of webhook URLs are kept.

| Source | App permission | Checks that read it |
|---|---|---|
| Organization settings | Organization permissions → Administration: Read-only | GID-001, GID-002, GID-003, GID-005, GID-006, GID-007 |
| Organization owners | Organization permissions → Members: Read-only | GID-004 |
| Actions permissions | Organization permissions → Administration: Read-only | GAC-001, GAC-002, GAC-003 |
| Organization webhooks | Organization permissions → Webhooks: Read-only | GHK-001, GHK-002 |
| Installed GitHub Apps | Organization permissions → Administration: Read-only | GHK-004 |
| Workflow policy for fork pull requests | Organization permissions → Administration: Read-only | GAC-004 |
| Self-hosted runners and runner groups | Organization permissions → Self-hosted runners: Read-only | GAC-005 |
| Repositories | Repository permissions → Metadata: Read-only (always granted) | Supporting data for other checks |
| Code security settings | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GSC-001, GSC-002, GSC-006 |
| Branch protection | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GBR-001, GBR-002, GBR-004, GBR-003 |
| Rulesets that apply to default branches | Repository permissions → Metadata: Read-only (always granted) | GBR-001, GBR-002, GBR-004, GBR-003 |
| Deploy keys | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GHK-003 |
| Repository webhooks | Repository permissions → Webhooks: Read-only | GHK-001, GHK-002 |
| GitHub Pages sites | Repository permissions → Pages: Read-only | GPG-001 |
| Public repositories' own self-hosted runners | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GAC-005 |
| Whether public repositories publish releases | None: a public repository's releases are public | GRL-001 |
| Whether releases are immutable | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GRL-001 |
| Whether Dependabot alerts are on | Repository permissions → Administration: Read-only | GSC-004, GSC-007 |
| Whether code scanning has run | Repository permissions → Code scanning alerts: Read-only | GSC-005, GSC-008 |
| Dependabot alerts | Repository permissions → Dependabot alerts: Read-only | GSC-004, GSC-006 |
| Code scanning alerts | Repository permissions → Code scanning alerts: Read-only | GSC-005 |
| Secret scanning alerts | Repository permissions → Secret scanning alerts: Read-only | GSC-003 |
